claims.text: Longhorn runs inside the Kubernetes cluster, builds volumes from disk space on the cluster's own nodes and keeps a copy (replica) of each volume on several nodes; it installs its own CSI driver, driver.longhorn.io.
claims.source_hint: longhorn.io docs 1.9: What is Longhorn?; Concepts > Architecture; don-hang stage-3 deploy/k8s/bare-metal/longhorn-storageclass.yaml L10-11

claims.text: The numberOfReplicas StorageClass parameter sets how many replicas each Longhorn volume gets; by default Longhorn places each replica of a volume on a different node (replica node-level soft anti-affinity off).
claims.source_hint: longhorn.io docs 1.9: References > Storage Class Parameters (numberOfReplicas); Settings > Replica Node Level Soft Anti-Affinity (default false)

claims.text: With the default (v1) data engine, each volume's engine runs on the Pod's node, receives its reads and writes and replicates each write synchronously to all healthy replicas, some over the network, before the write completes; a replica that stops answering is marked failed and no longer waited for.
claims.source_hint: longhorn.io docs 1.9: Concepts > Architecture (Longhorn Engine, synchronous replication to replicas)

claims.text: Each write on a Longhorn volume also waits for the replicas on other nodes, across the network, before it completes, so it takes longer than the same write would if it only had to reach the node's own disk.
claims.source_hint: longhorn.io docs 1.9: Concepts > Architecture (synchronous replication); Best Practices / performance notes

claims.text: A volume from kind's standard class (rancher.io/local-path) is a folder on one node, and its PersistentVolume is tied to that node, so the claim can be used only by a Pod on that node.
claims.source_hint: github.com/rancher/local-path-provisioner README (local volumes, node affinity); kubernetes.io: Persistent Volumes > Node Affinity

claims.text: Kubernetes does not replace a StatefulSet Pod on a failed node by itself; the stuck Pod must be deleted (Longhorn's Pod Deletion Policy When Node is Down, default do-nothing). Once replaced elsewhere, the volume attaches there: a new engine uses the remaining healthy replicas.
claims.source_hint: longhorn.io docs 1.9: High Availability > Node Failure Handling; Settings > Pod Deletion Policy When Node is Down; Concepts > Volume (degraded state)

claims.text: Longhorn rebuilds a missing replica from a healthy one on a node holding no replica of that volume; with default node-level anti-affinity, on three nodes with three replicas and one node down, the volume stays degraded until a node is free.
claims.source_hint: longhorn.io docs 1.9: Concepts > Replica rebuilding; Settings > Replica Node Level Soft Anti-Affinity; Volume degraded state

claims.text: Longhorn's default data engine (v1) needs an iSCSI initiator (open-iscsi, iscsid running) on every node; the lab does not set this up on its kind nodes, which is why it does not install Longhorn.
claims.source_hint: longhorn.io docs 1.9: Deploy > Installation Requirements (open-iscsi); don-hang stage-3 longhorn-storageclass.yaml L2-3

claims.text: provisioner driver.longhorn.io: Longhorn's CSI driver creates the volume for a claim naming longhorn-replicated; reclaimPolicy Delete: deleting the claim deletes the volume and all replicas; volumeBindingMode Immediate: provisioned once the claim exists; allowVolumeExpansion: claim can be enlarged.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Storage Classes > Provisioner, Reclaim Policy, Volume Binding Mode, Allow Volume Expansion; Persistent Volumes > Delete; longhorn.io docs 1.9: Storage Class Parameters

claims.text: On staging, the db StatefulSet keeps PostgreSQL's data on a claim from kind's standard class; db and rabbitmq each keep the only copy of their data on a claim; staging does not use Longhorn.
claims.source_hint: don-hang stage-3 deploy/gitops/config-repo-kustomize/base/db.yaml, rabbitmq.yaml (volumeClaimTemplates, no storageClassName); lesson k8s.l2.database-in-the-cluster

claims.text: All replicas of a Longhorn volume are in the same cluster and receive the same writes, so a bad write, deleting the volume or losing the cluster affects every replica; backups off the cluster are still needed.
claims.source_hint: longhorn.io docs 1.9: Concepts (replicas vs backups; Backup and Restore introduction)

claims.text: When PostgreSQL already streams its changes to a standby with its own volume, replicated volumes under both add copies of the same data and slower writes for little gain, when the team already fails over to the standby; they add most to stores that keep one copy.
